Subject: Benchmarking runbook + SLA checklist for Zephyrus pilot

Hi Andrew —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As discussed, I put together a short runbook to align on the acceptance testing we'll run during onboarding so we can finalize go/no-go before you cut traffic to our Dedicated pool. Attached is the working spreadsheet; below are the key items and the proposed cadence.

Summary of targets (proposal)
- Latency: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms for 1k token prompt (production prompt mix)
- Throughput: sustained 70–90 requests/sec per model replica under typical prompt distribution (burst headroom to 200 rps across the pool)
- Resource signal: GPU utilization target 60–75% steady-state during throughput test (to ensure headroom)
- Error budget: endpoint error rate <= 0.2% (5xx + rate-limited failures)

Planned tests and order
1) Smoke (dry run) — small-scale correctness and routing checks (1h)
2) Ramp & steady-state throughput (artifact: steady-state CSV) — ramp to 100% target over 30m, hold 60m
3) Latency tail analysis — synthetic mix + live prefix cache disabled/enabled to measure cache effect
4) Failure injection (network spikes, ablated cache) — confirm graceful fallbacks
5) Post-test sanity and token-cost reconciliation

Data & artifacts we need from your side
- A 200–300 prompt sample reflecting production distribution (anonymized)
- Target concurrency expected at cutover (per-region)
- Any disallowed prompt classes for eval sets (PII/PCI examples)

Next steps (action owners)
- Andrew: share anonymized prompt set and expected cutover traffic (by Tue 3/9)
- Marissa: schedule two 2-hour benchmarking windows (we suggest 3/7 and 3/9)
- Connor & Neha: confirm quantization profile and instance spec we'll use for Dedicated pool for the runs

Attachments: zephyrus-benchmark-runbook-v1.xlsx (has test scripts, JMeter templates, and metric dashboards to import to Grafana).

If that looks good I'll lock the 3/7/3/9 windows and run the smoke test on the 7th.

Cheers,

Quick tech notes from the smoke and first ramp run this morning (we executed the 09:00 PT window as scheduled):

Summary (first-run observations)
- Config used: q4fa model variant, 2xA10G nodes, batch size target 8, continuous batching on
- Observed steady-state throughput: 82 rps per replica (sustained for 35m on the hold period)
- Latency: p50 72ms, p95 198ms for the provided prompt sample (cache enabled)
- Tail behavior on uncached flows: p95 increased to 310ms when cache disabled; p99 spikes to ~540ms during cold-paths
- Error rate: 0.06% (one 502 due to transient GPU OOM during a synthetic malformed request)

Artifacts uploaded: initial-load-results-20260307.log (small results CSV + Grafana snapshot) — link in the runbook.

Notes and recommended follow-ups
- To reach Andrew's desired p95 <= 200ms on uncached heavy-tail flows we should: a) enable a slightly higher batch limit during peak (improves GPU throughput) and b) add a small warmup traffic pre-roll for cold workers prior to cutover.
- We need Zephyrus to confirm expected long-context requests percentage; if >10% we recommend the long-context kernel flag and a third node type optimized for attention memory layout.

I'll push a short test-automation update to the runbook (runnable JMeter flag to toggle cache). Planning the second run on 3/9 afternoon.

Connor
